How this is measured

Your pitch, read about 60 times a second, sets your height: the bottom of the course is the low end of your saved range and the top its high end. Go quiet and you fall. Your score is how far you flew; a coin counts when you pass it near the middle of a gap, and each one in a row adds to your combo.

By section

How this is measured

Each chord of the song is one note of the Lead line to sing. Your pitch is read about 60 times a second and compared with that note, natural vibrato taken out; a note you sing within the boss's threshold hurts the boss, a miss hurts you. Each boss judges a different thing: a steady hold, a note a fifth up, only the first half-second, your register, steady loudness, landing on time, or controlled vibrato.

Overall

Best—
Pitch—

Part accuracy—
Independence—
How this is measured

Your part's line is the target, note by note, natural vibrato taken out. Pitch is how close you sang across the piece; Timing is how much of it you were heard; Part accuracy is the share of notes you landed within about 40 cents; Independence is Pitch, weighted up by how loud the other parts were at your level. Overall is the average of the four.

Skill Tree

Each skill opens when your scores reach its mark, and can close again if they drop.

The Rift

Sixty seconds of rounds you can't predict: match a note, jump an interval, hold one steady, or catch one fast.

Rounds0 Average— Time60
—
—

—

Average

Best—
How this is measured

Each round picks one of four kinds at random and a note from your range, plays it, then listens: a note held 1.4 s, an interval from the last note, a 2.4 s hold, or a 0.65 s catch. Each round is scored like Pitch Match, from how close your pitch sat to the note. Your average is over the rounds where a pitch was heard.

Register Canyon

Chest voice runs the low lane, head voice the high one. Switch to dodge the blocks; three hits and the run ends.

Score0 Lives3 Best0

0

Score

Best—
How this is measured

Each frame reads your register, chest or head, from how your voice's energy sits across its harmonics: the same reading as Register Coach. Chest puts you in the low lane, head in the high one; with no voice you stay where you were. Blocks come in either lane at random; your score is how far you ran.

Average stability

How this is measured

Stability is 100 minus three times how much your pitch wavers, in cents, over its last 30 readings (about half a second). This number is the average for the whole time you sang. The ring locks when you're within 6 cents of the note.

Uses your microphone locally in the browser — nothing is uploaded. Best with headphones or a quiet room.

    Genuinely different from every other tool here — this measures WHEN you sing, not pitch. Real onset detection against a real metronome, not a fixed animation.
